title: RayCast3D can miss objects under a common parent node when only that parent node is translated
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.2.1 4.3 4.4

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable (77dcf97d8) - NixOS #1-NixOS SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Sep 12 09:13:13 UTC 2024 - X11 - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1240P (16 Threads)

### Issue description

If I create a Node3D and add a StaticBody3D and a RayCast3D as children and orient them in such a way that the RayCast3D collides with the centre of the StaticBody3D, it is possible for it to fail to collide if the Node3D is translated by more than the radius of StaticBody3D.

This is unexplained behavior because at all times in GDScript the difference `$RayCast3D.global_position - $StaticBody3D.global_position` is constant if they are only changed by the position of the Node3D.  

Yet somehow the position of the parengt Node3D is applied to `$RayCast3D.global_position` first, then the raycast is evaluated, *before* the StaticBody3D.global_position is updated.

I can tell it is happening this way, and it's not a culling error, or the StaticBody is moving first, because I have put a second fixed StaticBody3D just at the point where the ray misses that it hits instead, which proves that the StaticBody is being left behind during the update and raycast.

---

I found out this problem when a player was interacting with a radial menu in VR that was fixed in their coordinate space, and they couldn't hit if they happened to be falling.

### Steps to reproduce

The RayCast3D is aligned with the Y-axis and the StaticBody3D has a CollisionShape3D that is a BoxShape of size (1,1,1) 

The script on the Node3D containing them is:

```GDScript
extends Node3D

var vel = 1.0
func _physics_process(delta):
	var c = $RayCast3D.get_collider()
	if c == $StaticBody3D:
		pass  # this is expected
	else:
		print("raycast hits ", c)
		print("at velocity ", vel)
		print("physics step distance ", delta*vel)
		print("Static body global position ", $StaticBody3D.global_position)
		print("Raycast global position ", $RayCast3D.global_position)
	position.x += delta*vel
	vel += 10*delta
```

This prints:

```
raycast hits <Object#null>
at velocity 30.3333333333334
physics step distance 0.50555555555556
Static body global position (45.71111, 0, 0)
Raycast global position (45.71111, 1, 0)
```

Everything is aligned whenever you execute the GDScript.  It doesn't matter if the nodes are reordered or the StaticBody is made a child of the RayCast.  Somehow the RayCast position is updated first and independently of all the nodes in the tree before it intersects the objects with which there should be no relative movement.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[raycasttest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18580283/raycasttest.zip)
